title: Week 6 Worklog
content:
Week 6 Objectives: Complete full-stack integration across the 3-Tier Resilient Web Architecture: Ingress (ALB & CloudFront) $\rightarrow$ Compute (Private Auto Scaling EC2) $\rightarrow$ Persistence (Amazon RDS MySQL & S3). Deploy an active dynamic web application reading product catalogs directly from RDS MySQL and delivering media assets through Amazon CloudFront. Enforce secret management governance using AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store (SecureString with KMS encryption). Conduct comprehensive resilience drills (Full-stack Fault Tolerance & Multi-AZ RDS Failover Test). Perform the mid-term milestone evaluation, publish the synchronized Hugo worklog portal on GitHub Pages, and outline phase 2 objectives. Weekly Task Summary: Day Primary Tasks Start Date Completion Date Reference Material 2 End-to-End 3-Tier Integration: Stitch together ALB in Public Subnets $\rightarrow$ Private EC2 Compute $\rightarrow$ Private RDS MySQL through chained Security Groups. 19/10/2026 19/10/2026 AWS 3-Tier Architecture Pattern 3 Dynamic Web Deployment & SSM Parameters: Deploy product catalog application code and retrieve database credentials securely via SSM Parameter Store. 20/10/2026 20/10/2026 AWS Systems Manager Guide 4 Amazon CloudFront CDN & S3 OAC Setup: Configure multi-origin CloudFront distributions (ALB for dynamic routes, S3 with Origin Access Control for static media). 21/10/2026 21/10/2026 CloudFront OAC Guide 5 Comprehensive Resilience & Failover Testing: Execute an automated Reboot with Failover on RDS Multi-AZ, verify zero data loss, and monitor CloudWatch metrics. 22/10/2026 22/10/2026 Amazon RDS Multi-AZ Failover 6 Mid-Term Milestone Review & Documentation Sync: Evaluate halfway milestone goals, finalize Hugo documentation on GitHub Pages, and map out Phase 2 plans. 23/10/2026 23/10/2026 FCAJ Progress Review Detailed Technical Log: Monday (19/10/2026): End-to-End 3-Tier Architectural Integration Traffic Flow and Multi-Tier Topology:
Public Client Traffic $\rightarrow$ Application Load Balancer (10.10.1.0/24, 10.10.2.0/24 - Public Subnets). Ingress ALB $\rightarrow$ Auto Scaling EC2 Fleet (10.10.11.0/24, 10.10.12.0/24 - Isolated Private App Subnets). Compute Nodes $\rightarrow$ Amazon RDS MySQL (10.10.11.0/24, 10.10.12.0/24 - Isolated Private DB Subnets). Compute Nodes $\rightarrow$ Amazon S3 (routed securely via internal S3 Gateway Endpoints). Security Group Chaining Verification:
Audited ingress rules to enforce strict boundary defense: ALB-SG: Permits inbound port 80 (HTTP) and 443 (HTTPS) from 0.0.0.0/0. Web-App-SG: Restricts inbound port 80 exclusively to ALB-SG ID (rendering the compute layer immune to direct outside probes). Database-SG: Restricts inbound port 3306 exclusively to Web-App-SG ID (ensuring no traffic can touch database ports from outside the application tier). Tuesday (20/10/2026): Dynamic Web App Deployment & Parameter Store Hardening Secret Decoupling with AWS Systems Manager:
Completely eliminated hardcoded database credentials from source files and environment blocks. Initialized encrypted parameters in SSM Parameter Store: # Store connection endpoints and KMS-encrypted credentials aws ssm put-parameter \ --name "/app/production/db_endpoint" \ --value "duy-production-mysql.xxxxxx.ap-southeast-1.rds.amazonaws.com" \ --type "String" --overwrite aws ssm put-parameter \ --name "/app/production/db_password" \ --value "SuperSecurePassword2026!" \ --type "SecureString" --overwrite Bound IAM permissions (ssm:GetParameter and kms:Decrypt) to the EC2 IAM Instance Profile so compute nodes retrieve configuration upon application startup. Dynamic Application Code Implementation:
Built an interactive catalog view querying records dynamically from the RDS MySQL persistence tier: <?php require 'vendor/autoload.php'; use Aws\Ssm\SsmClient; $ssm = new SsmClient(['region' => 'ap-southeast-1', 'version' => 'latest']); $db_host = $ssm->getParameter(['Name' => '/app/production/db_endpoint'])['Parameter']['Value']; $db_pass = $ssm->getParameter(['Name' => '/app/production/db_password', 'WithDecryption' => true])['Parameter']['Value']; $conn = new mysqli($db_host, 'admin_duy', $db_pass, 'ecom_store_db', 3306); if ($conn->connect_error) { die("DB Connection Failed: " . $conn->connect_error); } $result = $conn->query("SELECT sku, name, price, stock_quantity FROM products"); echo "<h2>🔥 Live Product Catalog (Queried from Amazon RDS MySQL)</h2>"; echo "<table border='1' cellpadding='8' style='border-collapse: collapse; margin: auto;'>"; echo "<tr><th>SKU</th><th>Product Name</th><th>Price (USD)</th><th>Stock</th></tr>"; while($row = $result->fetch_assoc()) { echo "<tr><td>{$row['sku']}</td><td>{$row['name']}</td><td>\${$row['price']}</td><td>{$row['stock_quantity']}</td></tr>"; } echo "</table>"; ?> Wednesday (21/10/2026): Amazon CloudFront Multi-Origin & S3 OAC Hardening Multi-Origin Distribution Architecture:
Origin 1 (Dynamic Ingress): Points to the Application Load Balancer DNS (duy-public-alb-xxxx.elb.amazonaws.com). Behavior: Default wildcard pattern (*). Cache Policy: CachingDisabled (Passes all live catalog requests straight to compute nodes). Origin 2 (Static Media Assets): Points to the private S3 Bucket (duy-project-app-assets-2026.s3.ap-southeast-1.amazonaws.com). Behavior: Dedicated media path (/images/*). Cache Policy: CachingOptimized (Caches static images across global Edge Locations for 24 hours). Securing Storage via Origin Access Control (OAC):
Enabled S3 Block Public Access completely on the bucket. Configured CloudFront Origin Access Control (OAC) and attached the restricted S3 policy: { "Version": "2012-10-17", "Statement": { "Sid": "AllowCloudFrontServicePrincipalReadOnly", "Effect": "Allow", "Principal": { "Service": "cloudfront.amazonaws.com" }, "Action": "s3:GetObject", "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::duy-project-app-assets-2026/*", "Condition": { "StringEquals": { "AWS:SourceArn": "arn:aws:cloudfront::123456789012:distribution/E12345EXAMPLE" } } } } Thursday (22/10/2026): Full-Stack Resilience & Multi-AZ RDS Failover Drill RDS Multi-AZ Failover Validation Drill:
Launched continuous HTTP polling against the application endpoint at 1-second intervals. Initiated a disruptive event via the RDS Console: Selected instance duy-production-mysql $\rightarrow$ Reboot with Failover. Diagnostic Observations: Seconds 0 - 25: Application continued serving cached catalog assets seamlessly. Seconds 26 - 38: Transient connection failure observed while the active database promoted the standby node in AZ-2. Seconds 39+: RDS internal DNS record propagated to the promoted node’s IP; application connections re-established automatically without manual intervention. Result: Actual observed RTO registered at ~38 seconds, comfortably beating the 2-minute SLA target with Zero Data Loss. CloudWatch Metrics Analysis:
Inspected operational telemetry: ALB RequestCount: ~1,500 test requests recorded. TargetResponseTime: Sustained average of 18ms. CloudFront CacheHitRate: Maintained 86% efficiency on static /images/* paths. Friday (23/10/2026): Mid-Term Milestone Review & Documentation Publication Mid-Term Evaluation: Reached 100% of Phase 1 learning milestones: Transitioned from basic AWS CLI onboarding to orchestrating an enterprise-grade 3-Tier Resilient Web Architecture. Established complete working mastery over VPCs, Subnets, Gateways, ALBs, ASGs, Multi-AZ RDS, S3, CloudFront OAC, KMS, and SSM Parameter Store. Synchronizing Documentation: Standardized and published all Weekly Worklogs (Weeks 1 through 6) on the Hugo-powered internship portal. Validated site links and multi-language routing on GitHub Pages: https://nlvduyy180404-coder.github.io/NguyenLeVanDuy/. Roadmap for Phase 2 (Weeks 7 through 12): Translate manual architecture into Infrastructure as Code (IaC) with Terraform / CloudFormation. Architect automated CI/CD Pipelines using GitHub Actions to deploy application updates automatically. Finalize the comprehensive, publication-grade Workshop module. Week 6 Achievements: Realized Complete 3-Tier Architecture: Successfully tied together Ingress (CloudFront/ALB), Compute (Multi-AZ Private Auto Scaling EC2), and Database (Multi-AZ RDS MySQL). High-Performance Edge Caching: Configured multi-origin CDN caching with Origin Access Control, protecting S3 assets while realizing an 86% cache hit ratio. Enterprise Security Standards: Eliminated credential leaks via KMS-encrypted SSM Parameter Store integration; restricted database access purely to internal application tiers. Empirically Proven High Availability: Conducted live RDS Multi-AZ failover drills achieving recovery within ~38 seconds without data loss. Exemplary Mid-Term Documentation: Closed Phase 1 with a thoroughly validated, bilingual internship logbook published on GitHub Pages. Challenges Encountered & Solutions: Problem Encountered Root Cause Solution Implemented Web application thrown Access Denied when reading SSM parameters The EC2 IAM Role had ssm:GetParameter permission but lacked kms:Decrypt access to decrypt SecureString types. Appended kms:Decrypt permissions to the instance role’s policy document targeting the default Systems Manager KMS key. 403 Forbidden errors when CloudFront pulled media from S3 S3 Bucket Policy had a mismatched CloudFront Distribution ARN in the condition statement, or OAC was misbound. Audited the exact Distribution ARN inside the S3 policy’s Condition block and verified OAC profile assignment within CloudFront Origin Settings. Application crashed permanently during RDS failover Initial application code lacked retry connection logic, terminating the script upon the first socket disconnect. Implemented exponential backoff and retry handling in the database connection layer, allowing the app to poll and reconnect cleanly once DNS updated. Lessons Learned & Best Practices: Centralized Secret Governance: Never commit database passwords or API keys to source repositories. Utilize SSM Parameter Store or Secrets Manager with KMS encryption to simplify credential rotation. Synergy of CloudFront + ALB: CloudFront is not solely for static sites; pairing it in front of an ALB accelerates dynamic API traffic across AWS backbone edge networks and provides baseline DDoS mitigation (AWS Shield Standard). Resilience Requires Real Testing: High availability cannot be assumed without real chaos drills. Performing live failover simulations uncovers subtle edge cases like connection timeouts and DNS caching policies. Roadmap for Phase 2 (Weeks 7 through 12): Codify the entire 3-Tier infrastructure into Terraform (Infrastructure as Code). Build automated CI/CD Pipelines with GitHub Actions for zero-downtime application deployments. Author and publish the detailed, step-by-step Workshop capstone module.

title: Week 5 Worklog
content:
Week 5 Objectives: Implement secure one-way outbound Internet egress for private workloads utilizing AWS NAT Gateways. Optimize internal data traffic paths and reduce bandwidth expenses with Amazon S3 Gateway Endpoints (VPC Endpoints). Provision and secure a production-ready Amazon RDS MySQL relational database inside private subnets featuring AWS KMS encryption at rest. Validate end-to-end private network connectivity between private EC2 compute instances and the internal database endpoint. Conduct a comprehensive network security audit and establish strict cost-governance routines for fee-accruing networking services. Weekly Task Summary: Day Primary Tasks Start Date Completion Date Reference Material 2 NAT Gateway & Private Egress Routing: Provision a NAT Gateway in the Public Subnet and update Private Route Tables for secure outbound patch access. 12/10/2026 12/10/2026 VPC NAT Gateway Guide 3 S3 Gateway Endpoint Optimization: Configure a VPC Gateway Endpoint to Amazon S3, routing traffic through the AWS private network backbone without NAT charges. 13/10/2026 13/10/2026 AWS PrivateLink & Gateway Endpoints 4 Database Tier Provisioning (Amazon RDS): Create a multi-AZ DB Subnet Group and deploy a MySQL instance in private subnets with KMS storage encryption. 14/10/2026 14/10/2026 Amazon RDS User Guide 5 Application-to-Database Integration Testing: Install MySQL Client on private EC2, connect via internal DNS, initialize database schemas and mock records. 15/10/2026 15/10/2026 Connecting to an RDS Instance 6 Security Auditing & Cost Decommissioning: Perform external port penetration tests, evaluate internal query latencies, and tear down NAT Gateways and Elastic IPs. 16/10/2026 16/10/2026 AWS Security Best Practices Detailed Technical Log: Monday (12/10/2026): NAT Gateway Deployment & Private Subnet Egress Provisioning the NAT Gateway:
Allocated a dedicated static public Elastic IP (EIP). Deployed the NAT Gateway inside Public Subnet AZ1 (10.10.1.0/24): Name: Duy-Project-NATGW-AZ1 Subnet: Duy-Public-Subnet-AZ1 Elastic IP allocation ID: eipalloc-xxxxxx Monitored status transition from Pending $\rightarrow$ Available. Configuring the Private Route Table:
Created a dedicated custom route table named Duy-Private-RT. Added outbound default route: Destination: 0.0.0.0/0 (all outbound Internet traffic) Target: NAT Gateway (nat-xxxxxx) Associated both Private Subnets (10.10.11.0/24 and 10.10.12.0/24) with this route table. Verifying Outbound-Only Connectivity:
Launched a test EC2 instance strictly inside the Private Subnet (without assigning public IPv4). Accessed the instance via Bastion Host or AWS Systems Manager Session Manager. Verified one-way network egress: # Verify external DNS resolution and package manager downloads sudo dnf update -y # Verify outbound public IP matches the NAT Gateway Elastic IP curl https://checkip.amazonaws.com Validation confirmed: The internal host downloads packages freely while remaining completely shielded from unsolicited inbound Internet probes. Tuesday (13/10/2026): Architectural Optimization with S3 Gateway Endpoints Architectural Motivation:
Directing high-volume object transfers between private EC2 instances and Amazon S3 through a NAT Gateway incurs data processing fees (~$0.045/GB) and introduces network hops. Deploying a complimentary Gateway VPC Endpoint routes S3 traffic directly over the high-speed AWS Internal Network Backbone. Automating S3 Gateway Endpoint Creation via AWS CLI:
# Provision S3 Gateway Endpoint and associate directly with Private Route Table ENDPOINT_ID=$(aws ec2 create-vpc-endpoint \ --vpc-id $VPC_ID \ --service-name com.amazonaws.ap-southeast-1.s3 \ --route-table-ids $PRIVATE_RT_ID \ --tag-specifications 'ResourceType=vpc-endpoint,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=Duy-Project-S3-Endpoint}]' \ --query 'VpcEndpoint.VpcEndpointId' --output text) echo "Created S3 Gateway Endpoint: $ENDPOINT_ID" Routing Verification:
Inspected Duy-Private-RT; a new managed prefix list route was automatically injected: Destination: pl-xxxx (com.amazonaws.ap-southeast-1.s3) Target: vpce-xxxxxx Tested high-throughput object upload from private EC2 to S3: aws s3 cp large-data-file.tar.gz s3://duy-project-app-assets-2026/ Observed wire-speed transfer performance without incurring any NAT Gateway data-processing fees. Wednesday (14/10/2026): Deploying the Database Tier (Amazon RDS MySQL) DB Subnet Group Configuration:
Name: duy-project-rds-subnet-group VPC: Duy-Project-Production-VPC Attached Subnets: Selected 2 Private Subnets spanning distinct AZs (10.10.11.0/24 in ap-southeast-1a and 10.10.12.0/24 in ap-southeast-1b), ensuring full multi-AZ readiness. Hardening the RDS MySQL Instance:
Engine: MySQL Community 8.0. Template: Dev/Test tier. Identifiers: DB instance identifier: duy-production-mysql Master username: admin_duy Master password: [Securely managed in AWS Secrets Manager] Instance Specifications: Instance class: db.t4g.micro (Graviton2 ARM, 2 vCPU, 1 GB RAM). Storage: 20 GiB, Storage type: gp3. Network Isolation: VPC: Duy-Project-Production-VPC DB Subnet Group: duy-project-rds-subnet-group Publicly Accessible: No (Strictly internal). Security Group: Bound to Database-SG (Port 3306 restricted solely to Web-App-SG). Encryption: Storage encryption enabled via AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS key aws/rds). Thursday (15/10/2026): Private Tier Integration & Data Seeding Installing Database Client on Private Compute Node:
Connected to the private application EC2 instance. Installed the native client binary: sudo dnf install -y mariadb105 Establishing Connection via Private DNS Endpoint:
RDS_ENDPOINT="duy-production-mysql.xxxxxx.ap-southeast-1.rds.amazonaws.com" mysql -h $RDS_ENDPOINT -P 3306 -u admin_duy -p Database Schema Initialization & Data Population:
CREATE DATABASE ecom_store_db CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_unicode_ci; USE ecom_store_db; CREATE TABLE products ( id INT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY, sku VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL UNIQUE, name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL, price DECIMAL(10, 2) NOT NULL, stock_quantity INT DEFAULT 0, created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP ); INSERT INTO products (sku, name, price, stock_quantity) VALUES ('AWS-SHIRT-01', 'First Cloud AI Journey T-Shirt', 19.99, 100), ('AWS-HOODIE-02', 'Cloud Engineer Hoodie', 49.99, 50), ('AWS-MUG-03', 'Architect Ceramic Mug', 12.50, 200); SELECT * FROM products; Observations: Query operations completed instantaneously with local area network (LAN) round-trip latencies below 1 millisecond.
Friday (16/10/2026): Network Security Audit & Cost Hygiene Security Penetration Audit:
Attempted external port probing from an unauthenticated home workstation: telnet duy-production-mysql.xxxxxx.ap-southeast-1.rds.amazonaws.com 3306 Connection attempts timed out after 30 seconds with zero acknowledgement. Confirmed complete perimeter stealth: Port 3306 is utterly unreachable from the public Internet. Disciplined Decommissioning Routine:
NAT Gateway Teardown: Avoided the perpetual idle cost of $0.045/hour (~$32/month): # Delete NAT Gateway aws ec2 delete-nat-gateway --nat-gateway-id $NAT_GW_ID # Release unattached Elastic IP to avoid idle holding penalties ($0.005/hr) aws ec2 release-address --allocation-id $EIP_ALLOC_ID Stopped the RDS database instance during non-laboratory hours to preserve promotional credits. Week 5 Achievements: Production-Grade Private Networking: Successfully engineered one-way Internet access for private tier instances utilizing NAT Gateways and isolated route tables. Cost & Route Optimization via Endpoints: Configured Amazon S3 Gateway Endpoints, eliminating NAT data transfer costs while improving private throughput over the AWS backbone. Impenetrable Database Isolation: Deployed Amazon RDS MySQL within private subnet groups with KMS storage encryption, completely barring unauthorized public access. Verified Internal Tier Integration: Connected application compute instances to database endpoints over private DNS with sub-millisecond query latency. Proactive Cost Discipline: Decommissioned billable NAT Gateways and released unattached Elastic IPs immediately following validation. Challenges Encountered & Solutions: Problem Encountered Root Cause Solution Implemented Private instances unable to reach Internet after NAT Gateway creation The Private Route Table was missing the default 0.0.0.0/0 route directing outbound traffic to the newly created NAT Gateway. Edited the Private Route Table (Duy-Private-RT), added destination 0.0.0.0/0 targeting the NAT Gateway ID, and saved changes. Access Denied when private EC2 executed S3 commands via Endpoint The EC2 instance lacked an attached IAM Instance Profile granting programmatic S3 permissions. Created an IAM Role with AmazonS3FullAccess and associated it with the instance via Actions $\rightarrow$ Security $\rightarrow$ Modify IAM role. VPC deletion blocked due to DependencyViolation error NAT Gateway was still transitioning through deleting state, or active RDS Network Interfaces (ENIs) remained bound. Allowed the NAT Gateway to transition fully to deleted, dismantled the DB Subnet Group, and verified ENI detachment before deleting the VPC. Lessons Learned & Best Practices: Defense-in-Depth for Data Stores: Protecting relational databases demands 3 distinct defensive layers: (1) Placement in Private Subnets without Public IPs, (2) Security Groups restricted solely to app tier callers, (3) Data encryption at rest with AWS KMS. Beware Hidden Network Charges: Idle NAT Gateways and unattached Elastic IPs represent the most common sources of unexpected cloud spend. Always release Elastic IPs immediately upon NAT deletion. Architectural Value of VPC Endpoints: Gateway and Interface VPC Endpoints enhance both security (keeping data entirely on AWS wires) and cost efficiency (avoiding NAT data fees). Plan for Next Week (Week 6): Orchestrate the complete 3-Tier Integration: Application Load Balancer (Tier 1) $\rightarrow$ Auto Scaling EC2 (Tier 2) $\rightarrow$ Amazon RDS MySQL (Tier 3). Deploy a functional dynamic web application demo reading live data from RDS and rendering assets from S3. Execute full-stack end-to-end resilience and failover testing.

title: Week 4 Worklog
content:
Week 4 Objectives: Finalize the comprehensive Project Proposal report deliverable for the 3-Tier Resilient Web Architecture capstone project. Author an in-depth system architecture blueprint highlighting data paths and multi-Availability-Zone security boundaries. Model and forecast monthly operational expenditures using the official AWS Pricing Calculator. Perform risk matrix evaluations and formulate backup and disaster recovery (DR) strategies. Commence provisioning foundational cloud infrastructure components on AWS in accordance with the ratified architectural specifications. Weekly Task Summary: Day Primary Tasks Start Date Completion Date Reference Material 2 Proposal Authoring & Problem Statement: Articulate the business problem, target availability metrics (99.9% uptime SLA), and non-functional requirements. 05/10/2026 05/10/2026 Internal FCAJ Proposal Guide 3 Detailed Architecture Diagramming: Draft the 3-tier model (Ingress, Compute, Data Tiers) and establish Security Group chaining policies. 06/10/2026 06/10/2026 AWS Architecture Center 4 Budgeting via AWS Pricing Calculator: Break down granular costs across services (ALB, EC2, RDS Multi-AZ, S3, CloudFront). 07/10/2026 07/10/2026 AWS Pricing Calculator 5 Risk Assessment & DR Planning: Analyze risk exposure (RTO/RPO), finalize the formal deliverable, and conduct peer team review. 08/10/2026 08/10/2026 AWS Well-Architected Reliability 6 Foundational Infrastructure Provisioning: Stand up the Production VPC (4 Subnets across 2 AZs), attach an Internet Gateway, and create the S3 assets bucket. 09/10/2026 09/10/2026 Amazon VPC User Guide Detailed Technical Log: Monday (05/10/2026): Proposal Documentation & Business Problem Definition Context and Problem Statement: Small-to-medium enterprise applications and e-commerce platforms often encounter crippling server outages when traffic surges during flash sales or marketing campaigns. Traditional monolithic single-server deployments suffer from Single Points of Failure (SPOF): When an underlying physical host or datacenter network degrades, business operations halt. Defining Service Level Indicators & Targets (SLO / SLA): Availability: Target 99.9% uptime (under 8.76 hours of permissible unscheduled downtime annually). Elastic Scalability: Automated horizontal scaling from 2 up to 6 compute instances within 3 minutes when average CPU exceeds 60%. Disaster Recovery Targets: Recovery Point Objective (RPO): Under 5 minutes (transactional integrity preserved via RDS automated multi-AZ replication). Recovery Time Objective (RTO): Under 2 minutes (automatic health-check-driven failover without human intervention). Tuesday (06/10/2026): Detailed Architectural System Blueprinting 3-Tier Architectural Hierarchy:
Tier 1 - Ingress & Edge Tier: Amazon Route 53: Manages authoritative DNS resolution and intelligent health-checked routing. Amazon CloudFront: Global CDN caching static assets (HTML, CSS, JS, images) at worldwide edge locations, absorbing up to 70% of origin traffic. Application Load Balancer (ALB): Placed in Public Subnets across 2 Availability Zones, distributing HTTP/HTTPS traffic to application servers. Tier 2 - Application & Compute Tier: Auto Scaling Group (ASG): Manages fleets of Amazon EC2 nodes situated inside isolated Private App Subnets (devoid of public IPv4 addresses). NAT Gateway: Provides outbound-only Internet connectivity enabling private compute nodes to download security patches and updates. Tier 3 - Database & Storage Tier: Amazon RDS for MySQL (Multi-AZ Deployment): Primary DB host residing in Private Subnet AZ-1 with synchronous replication to an active Standby instance in AZ-2. Amazon S3 Bucket: Durable object storage for application media assets backed by 99.999999999% (11 9s) data durability. Security Group Chaining Matrix:
Security Group Permitted Inbound Traffic Source Rule Security Objective ALB-SG Port 80 (HTTP) / Port 443 (HTTPS) 0.0.0.0/0 (Internet) Ingress entrypoint for public client traffic Web-App-SG Port 80 (HTTP) ALB-SG ID only Eliminates unauthorized direct access bypassing the load balancer Database-SG Port 3306 (MySQL) Web-App-SG ID only Restricts database access strictly to authenticated compute instances Wednesday (07/10/2026): Quantitative Cost Modeling via AWS Pricing Calculator Detailed Monthly Expense Breakdown: Simulated realistic production workloads within the Singapore Region (ap-southeast-1): AWS Service Configuration Specifications Estimated Cost (USD/month) Amazon EC2 2x t3.micro instances (2 vCPU, 1GB RAM) running 24/7 baseline ~15.18 USD Amazon EBS 2x gp3 root volumes at 20GB each (40GB aggregate) ~3.20 USD Application Load Balancer 1 ALB processing ~10GB throughput and 1 LCU ~16.50 USD Amazon RDS (Multi-AZ) db.t4g.micro (2 vCPU, 1GB RAM) with 20GB gp3 storage ~26.40 USD Amazon S3 Standard 10GB object storage, 50,000 GET requests, 5,000 PUT requests ~0.45 USD Amazon CloudFront 50GB Data Transfer Out to Internet ~6.00 USD Data Transfer & Route 53 1 Public Hosted Zone + inter-AZ internal transfer ~1.50 USD Total Monthly Baseline (Prior to applying Free Tier promotions/credits) ~69.23 USD / month Development Sandbox Strategy: Leveraging the $200 Promotional Credit earned during previous onboarding milestones allows the team to sustain sandbox operations for over 2.5 months with zero out-of-pocket costs. For day-to-day development, deploying RDS in Single-AZ mode and pausing ALBs during inactive periods reduces operating spend by over 60%. Thursday (08/10/2026): Risk Assessment & Disaster Recovery Strategy Risk Evaluation Matrix: Identified Threat Impact Level Likelihood Mitigation Strategy Availability Zone (AZ) Outage Critical Low Multi-AZ architecture: ALB and ASG redirect traffic to surviving AZ; RDS executes automated failover within 60 seconds. Traffic Surges (Resource Starvation) High Medium ASG dynamic scale-out triggers when CPU > 60%; CloudFront CDN caches and serves static traffic from edge nodes. Database Corruption / Data Loss Severe Very Low Automated RDS point-in-time snapshots retained for 7 days; S3 object versioning enabled against accidental deletion. Unexpected Cost Overrun Moderate Low Configured AWS Budgets alerts dispatching notifications at 50%, 80%, and 100% project thresholds. Friday (09/10/2026): Foundational Infrastructure Provisioning Automated Production VPC Creation via AWS CLI:
# 1. Create project VPC with a 10.10.0.0/16 CIDR block VPC_ID=$(aws ec2 create-vpc --cidr-block 10.10.0.0/16 \ --tag-specifications 'ResourceType=vpc,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=Duy-Project-Production-VPC}]' \ --query 'Vpc.VpcId' --output text) echo "Created Production VPC: $VPC_ID" # 2. Enable DNS Hostnames inside the VPC aws ec2 modify-vpc-attribute --vpc-id $VPC_ID --enable-dns-hostnames "{\"Value\":true}" # 3. Create Internet Gateway and attach to VPC IGW_ID=$(aws ec2 create-internet-gateway \ --tag-specifications 'ResourceType=internet-gateway,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=Duy-Project-IGW}]' \ --query 'InternetGateway.InternetGatewayId' --output text) aws ec2 attach-internet-gateway --vpc-id $VPC_ID --internet-gateway-id $IGW_ID Network Subnet Allocation across 2 AZs (ap-southeast-1a & ap-southeast-1b):
Public Subnet AZ1: 10.10.1.0/24 (ALB Node A) Public Subnet AZ2: 10.10.2.0/24 (ALB Node B) Private Subnet AZ1: 10.10.11.0/24 (Compute Node A & RDS Primary) Private Subnet AZ2: 10.10.12.0/24 (Compute Node B & RDS Standby) Secure S3 Storage Provisioning:
# Provision the application asset repository bucket aws s3 mb s3://duy-project-app-assets-2026 --region ap-southeast-1 # Enable object versioning to safeguard against accidental overwrites aws s3api put-bucket-versioning \ --bucket duy-project-app-assets-2026 \ --versioning-configuration Status=Enabled Week 4 Achievements: Proposal Document Completed: Successfully authored the comprehensive Project Proposal deliverable detailing requirements, technical design, roadmap, and pricing. Professional Architecture Blueprint: Produced an industry-grade diagram illustrating multi-tier boundary separation, multi-AZ high availability, and Security Group chaining. Rigorous Cost Modeling: Mastered the AWS Pricing Calculator, accurately forecasting monthly operating expenses at ~$69 USD/month while demonstrating optimal utilization of promotional credits. Foundational Cloud Network Provisioned: Successfully stood up the production VPC spanning 4 subnets across two AZs with enabled DNS resolution and an attached Internet Gateway. Phase Readiness: Seamlessly transitioned from planning to execution, establishing a solid baseline for service provisioning in Week 5. Challenges Encountered & Solutions: Problem Encountered Root Cause Solution Implemented Multi-AZ RDS pricing exceeded initial estimates in Calculator Multi-AZ doubles compute hours and storage allocation to maintain the synchronous standby node. Adjusted development strategy: Use Single-AZ RDS (db.t4g.micro) during initial integration weeks; only activate Multi-AZ replication during final failover validation drills. CIDR address overlap when planning database subnets Subnet CIDR masks were initially too small or collided with legacy lab VPCs. Standardized on /24 subnet masks (251 usable host IPs per subnet) and created a dedicated address plan strictly separating public and private domains. CORS errors when CloudFront interacts with S3 assets S3 buckets restrict Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) by default for external domain origins. Attached a tailored JSON CORS policy to the S3 bucket allowing GET and HEAD methods from the CloudFront distribution domain. Lessons Learned & Best Practices: Architecture Planning Precedes Implementation: Spending adequate time designing network topology and modeling pricing mitigates costly tear-down and rebuild cycles later. Balancing Cost vs Availability: High availability requires deliberate architectural tradeoffs. Knowing when to run cost-effective dev configurations versus high-resilience production environments is an essential cloud engineering skill. Infrastructure as Code (IaC) Readiness: Scripting the VPC creation via AWS CLI builds the exact foundation needed for future automation with AWS CloudFormation or Terraform. Plan for Next Week (Week 5): Deploy the Compute Tier inside Private Subnets: Configure outbound Internet connectivity via NAT Gateway or VPC Endpoints. Launch the Amazon RDS MySQL instance inside the isolated private database subnet with KMS encryption at rest. Test internal application-to-database communication within the private network boundary.

title: Week 3 Worklog
content:
Week 3 Objectives: Collaborate with teammates and consult with Mentors to align on problem scope, requirements, and architecture for the Project Proposal. Master application-layer traffic distribution with Application Load Balancer (ALB), diving deep into Target Groups and Health Checks. Implement dynamic fleet elasticity using Auto Scaling Groups (ASG) and standardized Launch Templates. Tuesday (29/09/2026): Application Load Balancer (ALB) Configuration Target Group Provisioning:
Target type: Instances. Protocol: HTTP, Port: 80, VPC: Duy-Custom-VPC. Configured Health checks: Protocol: HTTP, Path: /index.html Healthy threshold: 3 consecutive successes. Unhealthy threshold: 2 consecutive failures. Timeout: 5 seconds, Interval: 15 seconds. Deploying the Application Load Balancer:
Name: Duy-Public-ALB. Scheme: Internet-facing. IP address type: IPv4. Network mapping: Selected Duy-Custom-VPC spanning 2 distinct Availability Zones: ap-southeast-1a $\rightarrow$ associated with Duy-Public-Subnet-AZ1 (10.0.1.0/24) ap-southeast-1b $\rightarrow$ associated with Duy-Public-Subnet-AZ2 (10.0.3.0/24) Security Group: Allowed inbound port 80 (HTTP) from 0.0.0.0/0. Registered 2 EC2 instances into the Target Group. Observed transition from Initial $\rightarrow$ Healthy. Visited the ALB DNS endpoint: http://duy-public-alb-12345678.ap-southeast-1.elb.amazonaws.com. Refreshing the browser confirmed alternating responses between backend instances, proving functional Round-Robin traffic distribution. Wednesday (30/09/2026): Dynamic Fleet Elasticity with Auto Scaling Group (ASG) Standardized Launch Template (Duy-Web-LT):
AMI: Amazon Linux 2023. Instance type: t2.micro (Free tier eligible). Security Group: Restricted inbound port 80 exclusively to the ALB’s Security Group ID (preventing direct bypass of the load balancer). Dynamic User Data bootstrap script leveraging IMDSv2 to output instance identity and zone location: #!/bin/bash dnf update -y dnf install -y httpd systemctl start httpd systemctl enable httpd # Retrieve Instance ID and Availability Zone via IMDSv2 session token TOKEN=`curl -X PUT "http://169.254.169.254/latest/api/token" -H "X-aws-ec2-metadata-token-ttl-seconds: 21600"` INSTANCE_ID=`curl -H "X-aws-ec2-metadata-token: $TOKEN" -s http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/instance-id` AZ=`curl -H "X-aws-ec2-metadata-token: $TOKEN" -s http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/placement/availability-zone` # Generate dynamic response webpage echo "<html><body style='font-family: Arial; text-align: center; margin-top: 50px;'>" > /var/www/html/index.html echo "<h1>🚀 Nguyen Le Van Duy - High Availability Web App</h1>" >> /var/www/html/index.html echo "<p>Served by Instance: <b>$INSTANCE_ID</b></p>" >> /var/www/html/index.html echo "<p>Running in Availability Zone: <span style='color: green;'><b>$AZ</b></span></p>" >> /var/www/html/index.html echo "</body></html>" >> /var/www/html/index.html Auto Scaling Group Configuration (Duy-Web-ASG):
Associated with Launch Template Duy-Web-LT. Subnet distribution: Multi-AZ across both Public Subnets. Load Balancer integration: Attached to Duy-Target-Group. Capacity quotas: Desired capacity: 2 Minimum capacity: 2 Maximum capacity: 4 Configured Target Tracking Scaling Policy: Metric: Average CPU utilization Target value: 50% (Automatically triggers scale-out actions when average CPU crosses 50%). Thursday (01/10/2026): Multi-AZ Fault Tolerance & Edge CDN Exploration Simulated High Load Stress Test (Scale-Out Verification):
Logged into an ASG-spawned EC2 instance via EC2 Instance Connect. Installed the Linux stress utility: sudo dnf install -y stress # Spawn 2 CPU-bound worker processes targeting 100% load for 300 seconds stress --cpu 2 --timeout 300 CloudWatch & ASG observation: Average CPU exceeded the 50% threshold within minutes. ASG initiated a Scaling Activity, automatically provisioning a 3rd instance and seamlessly registering it with the ALB without manual administrative intervention. Once the workload ceased and CPU normalized, the policy executed a Scale-in action, gracefully terminating excess nodes back to 2. Validating Self-Healing and Zero Downtime:
Manually terminated one EC2 instance directly in the AWS Console. Target Group health checks immediately flagged the instance as Unhealthy and ceased sending requests to it. Within seconds, ASG detected capacity drop (1 < Desired 2) and automatically provisioned a fresh replacement instance (Self-healing), preserving uptime without service interruption. Exploration of Amazon CloudFront & Amazon Route 53:
Studied how CloudFront’s worldwide Edge Location network caches static web assets (images, CSS, media), reducing round-trip latency and offloading origin load from the ALB. Reviewed Route 53 routing policies (Simple, Weighted, Latency, and Failover routing). Friday (02/10/2026): Proposal Finalization & Cost-conscious Teardown Consolidating Proposal Specifications: Completed the high-level architecture diagram and component definitions for the upcoming proposal milestone. Prepared service inventory: Amazon VPC, ALB, Auto Scaling EC2, Amazon RDS MySQL Multi-AZ, and Amazon S3. Allocated documentation sections across team members for the formal proposal deliverable. Safe Resource Teardown (Cost Governance): Set ASG Desired and Minimum capacity to 0, then deleted the Auto Scaling Group. Deleted the Application Load Balancer and Target Group. Removed temporary Security Groups to maintain a clean cloud environment and prevent accidental budget leakage. Week 3 Achievements: Load Balancing Mastery: Acquired concrete expertise configuring ALBs, Target Groups, and granular HTTP health check thresholds for early fault detection. Elastic Infrastructure Automation: Designed Launch Templates utilizing IMDSv2 metadata retrieval and orchestrated CPU-driven Target Tracking scaling policies. Validated High Availability & Resilience: Successfully verified the Self-healing capability of AWS Auto Scaling during simulated instance crashes. Ensured uninterrupted Zero Downtime availability across multiple geographic Availability Zones (Multi-AZ). Clear Capstone Project Direction: Unified team vision on a robust 3-Tier architecture proposal deliverable. Proactive Cost Discipline: Maintained strict hygiene by promptly decommissioning billable load balancers and auto scaling groups immediately following verification. Challenges Encountered & Solutions: Problem Encountered Root Cause Solution Implemented ALB reported instances as permanently Unhealthy Health checks expected /index.html, but Apache was slow to initialize, or the EC2 Security Group did not permit ALB ingress traffic. Verified the User Data script ensured systemctl start httpd executed successfully, and updated EC2 Inbound Rules to explicitly permit port 80 only from the ALB’s Security Group ID. User Data failed to retrieve Instance ID (IMDSv2 requirement) Amazon Linux 2023 defaults to IMDSv2, requiring a PUT session token before allowing metadata queries. Added a curl -X PUT token generation step with header X-aws-ec2-metadata-token-ttl-seconds before querying instance-id and placement/availability-zone. Auto Scaling reaction time felt delayed during stress tests Default CloudWatch metric collection intervals and cooldown/warm-up periods were set conservatively. Tuned evaluation periods and warmup duration in the Scaling Policy configuration to make responsiveness suitable for experimental validation. Lessons Learned & Best Practices: Security Group Chaining: Never expose compute instances directly to the public Internet (0.0.0.0/0). Restrict inbound traffic strictly to the security group of the front-facing Load Balancer. Design for Failure across Multi-AZ: Hardware failures are inevitable at cloud scale. Spanning compute clusters across at least two Availability Zones is mandatory for production-grade reliability. Operational Power of Instance Metadata (IMDSv2): Dynamically querying metadata empowers instances to inspect their own operating context (Zone, Region, ID), streamlining troubleshooting and distributed logging. Plan for Next Week (Week 4): Finalize and submit the formal Project Proposal Deliverable: Problem statement, detailed 3-tier architecture, and AWS Pricing Calculator budget analysis. Begin initial baseline infrastructure provisioning for the approved project design. Prepare presentation slides for the Proposal Defense before Mentors and FCAJ peers.

Weekly Task Summary: Day Primary Tasks Start Date Completion Date Reference Material 2 AWS CLI Setup & Identity Management: Generate IAM Access Keys, configure CLI profile, and test permissions via the terminal. 21/09/2026 21/09/2026 AWS CLI User Guide 3 Mastering Amazon S3 Storage: Create Globally Unique Buckets, manage objects via CLI, configure Block Public Access & Bucket Policies. 22/09/2026 22/09/2026 S3 Documentation 4 Amazon VPC Network Design: Plan CIDR address blocks, configure Public/Private Subnets, Internet Gateway, and Route Tables. 23/09/2026 23/09/2026 VPC User Guide 5 EC2 Bootstrap & EBS Storage: Launch EC2 with User Data to automate Web Server provisioning; attach, format, and mount new EBS volumes. 24/09/2026 24/09/2026 EC2 User Guide 6 Free Tier Milestones ($200 Credit): Provision an Amazon RDS relational database instance and establish budget alerts using AWS Budgets. 25/09/2026 25/09/2026 AWS Free Tier 2025 Detailed Technical Log: Monday (21/09/2026): AWS CLI Installation & Configuration Create Access Key for IAM User:
Log in to the IAM Console using the IAM User credentials established in Week 1. Navigate to Security credentials $\rightarrow$ select Create access key $\rightarrow$ select Command Line Interface (CLI) use case. Securely save the Access Key ID and Secret Access Key pair without exposing them publicly. Terminal Configuration:
# Launch the AWS CLI configuration wizard aws configure Provide the requested parameters: AWS Access Key ID: AKIA... AWS Secret Access Key: wJalrXUtnFEMI... Default region name: ap-southeast-1 (Singapore) Default output format: json Verify Identity & Connectivity:
aws sts get-caller-identity Expected JSON response:
{ "UserId": "AIDASAMPLEUSERID2026", "Account": "123456789012", "Arn": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:user/duy-iam-user" } Tuesday (22/09/2026): Object Storage Management with Amazon S3 Bucket Creation and Object Operations via CLI:
# Create a new bucket with a globally unique name aws s3 mb s3://fcj-duy-storage-bucket-2026 --region ap-southeast-1 # Upload a sample file to the bucket aws s3 cp sample-file.txt s3://fcj-duy-storage-bucket-2026/ # List objects inside the bucket aws s3 ls s3://fcj-duy-storage-bucket-2026/ Access Control (S3 Block Public Access & Bucket Policies):
By default, Amazon S3 enforces Block all public access at the account and bucket levels to safeguard against accidental data leaks. For specific report artifacts requiring public viewing, disabled Block Public Access and attached a well-scoped Bucket Policy: { "Version": "2012-10-17", "Statement": [ { "Sid": "PublicReadGetObject", "Effect": "Allow", "Principal": "*", "Action": "s3:GetObject", "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::fcj-duy-storage-bucket-2026/*" } ] } Wednesday (23/09/2026): Building a Custom Amazon VPC Architecture from Scratch Network Addressing Plan: Component Resource Name CIDR Block Description VPC Duy-Custom-VPC 10.0.0.0/16 Accommodates up to 65,536 private IP addresses Public Subnet Duy-Public-Subnet-AZ1 10.0.1.0/24 Associated with Route Table directing out to Internet Gateway Private Subnet Duy-Private-Subnet-AZ1 10.0.2.0/24 Isolated internal subnet designated for database instances Internet Gateway Duy-VPC-IGW - Bridge connecting the VPC to the public Internet Route Table Configuration for Public Subnet: Provisioned a custom Route Table named Duy-Public-RT. Added outbound routing rule: Destination: 0.0.0.0/0 (all outbound IPv4 traffic) Target: Internet Gateway (Duy-VPC-IGW) Associated Subnet 10.0.1.0/24 with this route table. Thursday (24/09/2026): EC2 Automation with User Data & EBS Volume Mounting Launch Virtual Machine with User Data Script:
Under Advanced details $\rightarrow$ User data during EC2 launch (Amazon Linux 2023), provided an automated bootstrap script: #!/bin/bash # Update software packages dnf update -y # Install Apache HTTP Server dnf install -y httpd # Enable and start the service systemctl start httpd systemctl enable httpd # Generate default test landing page echo "<h1>Welcome to Nguyen Le Van Duy's Web Server on AWS!</h1>" > /var/www/html/index.html As soon as the instance transitioned to Running, loading the Public IP in a web browser instantly rendered the test page without requiring manual SSH intervention. Attach and Mount a Secondary EBS Volume:
Created a 5GB General Purpose SSD (gp3) volume in the same Availability Zone as the EC2 instance. Selected Attach Volume to associate the block device with the EC2 instance. Connected via SSH to partition, format, and mount the storage: # Inspect block device tree lsblk # Create an ext4 filesystem on the new volume sudo mkfs -t ext4 /dev/xvdf # Create mount point directory and mount device sudo mkdir /data sudo mount /dev/xvdf /data # Verify filesystem disk space usage df -h /data Friday (25/09/2026): Completing Free Tier Milestones ($200 Credit) Deploy Relational Database with Amazon RDS:
Service: Amazon RDS $\rightarrow$ Create database. Engine: MySQL (Community Edition). Template: Free Tier (db.t3.micro or db.t4g.micro, 20GB gp2 storage). Placed the instance inside the VPC Private Subnet for security isolation, permitting inbound connections only from the EC2 Web Server Security Group over port 3306. Completed connection tests and immediately initiated Delete Database (without final snapshot) to conserve allocated Free Tier quotas. Configure Budget Tracking via AWS Budgets:
Navigated to AWS Billing and Cost Management $\rightarrow$ Budgets. Created a Cost Budget: Budget amount: $10 USD / month. Configured notification threshold: Automatically sends alert emails to nlvduyy180404@gmail.com when actual spending reaches 80% ($8 USD) or forecasted spending hits 100%. Successfully achieved all 5 hands-on milestones, crediting the full $200 promotional allowance to the account. Week 2 Achievements: CLI Competence: Gained proficiency using AWS CLI commands to query resources, configure multi-region profiles, and execute actions directly from the terminal without graphical console dependency. Storage Distinction: Mastered the architectural differences between Object Storage (S3 - files, static assets, backups) and Block Storage (EBS - raw virtual disks for operating systems and databases). Network Independence: Successfully designed and stood up an isolated Custom VPC network with separate Public/Private subnets and Internet Gateway routing. Infrastructure Automation: Demonstrated automated server bootstrapping using User Data scripts, drastically accelerating infrastructure provisioning. Financial Governance & Security: Completed all AWS Free Tier 2025 milestone challenges, earned the full $200 promotional credit, and established proactive budget alarms to avoid unexpected billing. Challenges Encountered & Solutions: Problem Encountered Root Cause Solution Implemented 403 Forbidden error when downloading objects via public S3 URLs S3 Block Public Access safeguards were enabled at the account and bucket levels to prevent data exposure. Disabled Block Public Access on the specific bucket and applied a JSON Bucket Policy granting s3:GetObject permissions to public users (*). Attached EBS volume not visible in Linux filesystem Raw block devices lack a filesystem and must be explicitly formatted and mounted into the Linux hierarchy. Ran lsblk to identify the device path, executed sudo mkfs -t ext4 to format the partition, and used sudo mount to link the volume to /data. Amazon RDS instance takes prolonged time to provision and fails connection Managed database provisioning inherently requires 5–10 minutes; the default security group blocks all incoming network traffic. Waited patiently until status displayed Available. Adjusted the DB Security Group to permit port 3306 inbound traffic from the EC2 Security Group. Promptly deleted the database after validation to prevent ongoing storage charges. Lessons Learned & Best Practices: Credential Hygiene: Never hardcode Access Keys or Secret Keys into application codebases or commit them to public GitHub repositories. Favor IAM Roles over long-lived access keys whenever AWS services communicate with one another (e.g., EC2 instance roles calling S3). Network Isolation Principles: Only position public-facing ingress components (e.g., Web Servers, Load Balancers) in Public Subnets. Keep databases (RDS) and internal processing services strictly inside Private Subnets to minimize potential attack surfaces. The Value of Automated Provisioning: Utilizing User Data bootstrap scripts eliminates human error associated with repetitive manual configuration and accelerates server readiness. Plan for Next Week (Week 3): Explore high-availability load balancing with Application Load Balancer (ALB). Study automated horizontal scaling with Auto Scaling Groups (ASG). Practice orchestrating VPC + ALB + EC2 Auto Scaling to construct a resilient, fault-tolerant web architecture.

title: Introduction
content:
VPC endpoints VPC endpoints are virtual devices. They are horizontally scaled, redundant, and highly available VPC components. They allow communication between your compute resources and AWS services without imposing availability risks. Compute resources running in VPC can access Amazon S3 using a Gateway endpoint. PrivateLink interface endpoints can be used by compute resources running in VPC or on-premises. Workshop overview In this workshop, you will use two VPCs.
“VPC Cloud” is for cloud resources such as a Gateway endpoint and an EC2 instance to test with. “VPC On-Prem” simulates an on-premises environment such as a factory or corporate datacenter. An EC2 instance running strongSwan VPN software has been deployed in “VPC On-prem” and automatically configured to establish a Site-to-Site VPN tunnel with AWS Transit Gateway. This VPN simulates connectivity from an on-premises location to the AWS cloud. To minimize costs, only one VPN instance is provisioned to support this workshop. When planning VPN connectivity for your production workloads, AWS recommends using multiple VPN devices for high availability.

title: Proposal
content:
⚠️ Note: The information below is for reference purposes only. Please do not copy verbatim for your report, including this warning.
In this section, you need to summarize the contents of the workshop that you plan to conduct.
IoT Weather Platform for Lab Research A Unified AWS Serverless Solution for Real-Time Weather Monitoring 1. Executive Summary The IoT Weather Platform is designed for the ITea Lab team in Ho Chi Minh City to enhance weather data collection and analysis. It supports up to 5 weather stations, with potential scalability to 10-15, utilizing Raspberry Pi edge devices with ESP32 sensors to transmit data via MQTT. The platform leverages AWS Serverless services to deliver real-time monitoring, predictive analytics, and cost efficiency, with access restricted to 5 lab members via Amazon Cognito.
2. Problem Statement What’s the Problem? Current weather stations require manual data collection, becoming unmanageable with multiple units. There is no centralized system for real-time data or analytics, and third-party platforms are costly and overly complex.
The Solution The platform uses AWS IoT Core to ingest MQTT data, AWS Lambda and API Gateway for processing, Amazon S3 for storage (including a data lake), and AWS Glue Crawlers and ETL jobs to extract, transform, and load data from the S3 data lake to another S3 bucket for analysis. AWS Amplify with Next.js provides the web interface, and Amazon Cognito ensures secure access. Similar to Thingsboard and CoreIoT, users can register new devices and manage connections, though this platform operates on a smaller scale and is designed for private use. Key features include real-time dashboards, trend analysis, and low operational costs.
Benefits and Return on Investment The solution establishes a foundational resource for lab members to develop a larger IoT platform, serving as a study resource, and provides a data foundation for AI enthusiasts for model training or analysis. It reduces manual reporting for each station via a centralized platform, simplifying management and maintenance, and improves data reliability. Monthly costs are $0.66 USD per the AWS Pricing Calculator, with a 12-month total of $7.92 USD. All IoT equipment costs are covered by the existing weather station setup, eliminating additional development expenses. The break-even period of 6-12 months is achieved through significant time savings from reduced manual work.
3. Solution Architecture The platform employs a serverless AWS architecture to manage data from 5 Raspberry Pi-based stations, scalable to 15. Data is ingested via AWS IoT Core, stored in an S3 data lake, and processed by AWS Glue Crawlers and ETL jobs to transform and load it into another S3 bucket for analysis. Lambda and API Gateway handle additional processing, while Amplify with Next.js hosts the dashboard, secured by Cognito. The architecture is detailed below:
AWS Services Used AWS IoT Core: Ingests MQTT data from 5 stations, scalable to 15. AWS Lambda: Processes data and triggers Glue jobs (two functions). Amazon API Gateway: Facilitates web app communication. Amazon S3: Stores raw data in a data lake and processed outputs (two buckets). AWS Glue: Crawlers catalog data, and ETL jobs transform and load it. AWS Amplify: Hosts the Next.js web interface. Amazon Cognito: Secures access for lab users. Component Design Edge Devices: Raspberry Pi collects and filters sensor data, sending it to IoT Core. Data Ingestion: AWS IoT Core receives MQTT messages from the edge devices. Data Storage: Raw data is stored in an S3 data lake; processed data is stored in another S3 bucket. Data Processing: AWS Glue Crawlers catalog the data, and ETL jobs transform it for analysis. Web Interface: AWS Amplify hosts a Next.js app for real-time dashboards and analytics. User Management: Amazon Cognito manages user access, allowing up to 5 active accounts. 4. Technical Implementation Implementation Phases This project has two parts—setting up weather edge stations and building the weather platform—each following 4 phases:
Build Theory and Draw Architecture: Research Raspberry Pi setup with ESP32 sensors and design the AWS serverless architecture (1 month pre-internship) Calculate Price and Check Practicality: Use AWS Pricing Calculator to estimate costs and adjust if needed (Month 1). Fix Architecture for Cost or Solution Fit: Tweak the design (e.g., optimize Lambda with Next.js) to stay cost-effective and usable (Month 2). Develop, Test, and Deploy: Code the Raspberry Pi setup, AWS services with CDK/SDK, and Next.js app, then test and release to production (Months 2-3). Technical Requirements
Weather Edge Station: Sensors (temperature, humidity, rainfall, wind speed), a microcontroller (ESP32), and a Raspberry Pi as the edge device. Raspberry Pi runs Raspbian, handles Docker for filtering, and sends 1 MB/day per station via MQTT over Wi-Fi. Weather Platform: Practical knowledge of AWS Amplify (hosting Next.js), Lambda (minimal use due to Next.js), AWS Glue (ETL), S3 (two buckets), IoT Core (gateway and rules), and Cognito (5 users). Use AWS CDK/SDK to code interactions (e.g., IoT Core rules to S3). Next.js reduces Lambda workload for the fullstack web app. 5. Timeline & Milestones Project Timeline
Pre-Internship (Month 0): 1 month for planning and old station review. Internship (Months 1-3): 3 months. Month 1: Study AWS and upgrade hardware. Month 2: Design and adjust architecture. Month 3: Implement, test, and launch. Post-Launch: Up to 1 year for research. 6. Budget Estimation You can find the budget estimation on the AWS Pricing Calculator.
Or you can download the Budget Estimation File.
Infrastructure Costs AWS Services: AWS Lambda: $0.00/month (1,000 requests, 512 MB storage). S3 Standard: $0.15/month (6 GB, 2,100 requests, 1 GB scanned). Data Transfer: $0.02/month (1 GB inbound, 1 GB outbound). AWS Amplify: $0.35/month (256 MB, 500 ms requests). Amazon API Gateway: $0.01/month (2,000 requests). AWS Glue ETL Jobs: $0.02/month (2 DPUs). AWS Glue Crawlers: $0.07/month (1 crawler). MQTT (IoT Core): $0.08/month (5 devices, 45,000 messages). Total: $0.7/month, $8.40/12 months
Hardware: $265 one-time (Raspberry Pi 5 and sensors). 7. Risk Assessment Risk Matrix Network Outages: Medium impact, medium probability. Sensor Failures: High impact, low probability. Cost Overruns: Medium impact, low probability. Mitigation Strategies Network: Local storage on Raspberry Pi with Docker. Sensors: Regular checks and spares. Cost: AWS budget alerts and optimization. Contingency Plans Revert to manual methods if AWS fails. Use CloudFormation for cost-related rollbacks. 8. Expected Outcomes Technical Improvements: Real-time data and analytics replace manual processes.
Scalable to 10-15 stations.
Long-term Value 1-year data foundation for AI research.
Reusable for future projects.

title: Access S3 from on-premises
content:
Overview In this section, you will create an Interface endpoint to access Amazon S3 from a simulated on-premises environment. The Interface endpoint will allow you to route to Amazon S3 over a VPN connection from your simulated on-premises environment.
Why using Interface endpoint:
Gateway endpoints only work with resources running in the VPC where they are created. Interface endpoints work with resources running in VPC, and also resources running in on-premises environments. Connectivty from your on-premises environment to the cloud can be provided by AWS Site-to-Site VPN or AWS Direct Connect. Interface endpoints allow you to connect to services powered by AWS PrivateLink. These services include some AWS services, services hosted by other AWS customers and partners in their own VPCs (referred to as PrivateLink Endpoint Services), and supported AWS Marketplace Partner services. For this workshop, we will focus on connecting to Amazon S3.

title: On-premises DNS Simulation
content:
AWS PrivateLink endpoints have a fixed IP address in each Availability Zone where they are deployed, for the life of the endpoint (until it is deleted). These IP addresses are attached to Elastic Network Interfaces (ENIs). AWS recommends using DNS to resolve the IP addresses for endpoints so that downstream applications use the latest IP addresses when ENIs are added to new AZs, or deleted over time.
In this section, you will create a forwarding rule to send DNS resolution requests from a simulated on-premises environment to a Route 53 Private Hosted Zone. This section leverages the infrastructure deployed by CloudFormation in the Prepare the environment section.
Create DNS Alias Records for the Interface endpoint Navigate to the Route 53 management console (Hosted Zones section). The CloudFormation template you deployed in the Prepare the environment section created this Private Hosted Zone. Click on the name of the Private Hosted Zone, s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com: Create a new record in the Private Hosted Zone: Record name and record type keep default options Alias Button: Click to enable Route traffic to: Alias to VPC Endpoint Region: US East (N. Virginia) [us-east-1] Choose endpoint: Paste the Regional VPC Endpoint DNS name from your text editor (you saved when doing section 4.3) Click Add another record, and add a second record using the following values. Click Create records when finished to create both records. Record name: *. Record type: keep default value (type A) Alias Button: Click to enable Route traffic to: Alias to VPC Endpoint Region: US East (N. Virginia) [us-east-1] Choose endpoint: Paste the Regional VPC Endpoint DNS name from your text editor The new records appear in the Route 53 console:
Create a Resolver Forwarding Rule Route 53 Resolver Forwarding Rules allow you to forward DNS queries from your VPC to other sources for name resolution. Outside of a workshop environment, you might use this feature to forward DNS queries from your VPC to DNS servers running on-premises. In this section, you will simulate an on-premises conditional forwarder by creating a forwarding rule that forwards DNS queries for Amazon S3 to a Private Hosted Zone running in “VPC Cloud” in-order to resolve the PrivateLink interface endpoint regional DNS name.
From the Route 53 management console, click Inbound endpoints on the left side bar In the Inbound endpoints console, click the ID of the inbound endpoint Copy the two IP addresses listed to your text editor From the Route 53 menu, choose Resolver > Rules, and click Create rule: In the Create rule console: Name: myS3Rule Rule type: Forward Domain name: s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com VPC: VPC On-prem Outbound endpoint: VPCOnpremOutboundEndpoint Target IP Addresses: Enter both IP addresses from your text editor (inbound endpoint addresses) and then click Submit You have successfully created resolver forwarding rule.
Test the on-premises DNS Simulation Connect to Test-Interface-Endpoint EC2 instance with Session manager Test DNS resolution. The dig command will return the IP addresses assigned to the VPC Interface endpoint running in VPC Cloud (your IP’s will be different): dig +short s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com The IP addresses returned are the VPC endpoint IP addresses, NOT the Resolver IP addresses you pasted from your text editor. The IP addresses of the Resolver endpoint and the VPC endpoint look similar because they are all from the VPC Cloud CIDR block.
Navigate to the VPC menu (Endpoints section), select the S3 Interface endpoint. Click the Subnets tab and verify that the IP addresses returned by Dig match the VPC endpoint: Return to your shell and use the AWS CLI to test listing your S3 buckets: aws s3 ls --endpoint-url https://s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com Terminate your Session Manager session: In this section you created an Interface endpoint for Amazon S3. This endpoint can be reached from on-premises through Site-to-Site VPN or AWS Direct Connect. Route 53 Resolver outbound endpoints simulated forwarding DNS requests from on-premises to a Private Hosted Zone running the cloud. Route 53 inbound Endpoints recieved the resolution request and returned a response containing the IP addresses of the VPC interface endpoint. Using DNS to resolve the endpoint IP addresses provides high availability in-case of an Availability Zone outage.

title: VPC Endpoint Policies
content:
When you create an interface or gateway endpoint, you can attach an endpoint policy to it that controls access to the service to which you are connecting. A VPC endpoint policy is an IAM resource policy that you attach to an endpoint. If you do not attach a policy when you create an endpoint, AWS attaches a default policy for you that allows full access to the service through the endpoint.
You can create a policy that restricts access to specific S3 buckets only. This is useful if you only want certain S3 Buckets to be accessible through the endpoint.
In this section you will create a VPC endpoint policy that restricts access to the S3 bucket specified in the VPC endpoint policy.
Connect to an EC2 instance and verify connectivity to S3 Start a new AWS Session Manager session on the instance named Test-Gateway-Endpoint. From the session, verify that you can list the contents of the bucket you created in Part 1: Access S3 from VPC: aws s3 ls s3://\<your-bucket-name\> The bucket contents include the two 1 GB files uploaded in earlier.
Create a new S3 bucket; follow the naming pattern you used in Part 1, but add a ‘-2’ to the name. Leave other fields as default and click create Successfully create bucket
Navigate to: Services > VPC > Endpoints, then select the Gateway VPC endpoint you created earlier. Click the Policy tab. Click Edit policy. The default policy allows access to all S3 Buckets through the VPC endpoint.
In Edit Policy console, copy & Paste the following policy, then replace yourbucketname-2 with your 2nd bucket name. This policy will allow access through the VPC endpoint to your new bucket, but not any other bucket in Amazon S3. Click Save to apply the policy. { "Id": "Policy1631305502445", "Version": "2012-10-17", "Statement": [ { "Sid": "Stmt1631305501021", "Action": "s3:*", "Effect": "Allow", "Resource": [ "arn:aws:s3:::yourbucketname-2", "arn:aws:s3:::yourbucketname-2/*" ], "Principal": "*" } ] } Successfully customize policy
From your session on the Test-Gateway-Endpoint instance, test access to the S3 bucket you created in Part 1: Access S3 from VPC aws s3 ls s3://<yourbucketname> This command will return an error because access to this bucket is not permitted by your new VPC endpoint policy:
Return to your home directory on your EC2 instance cd~ Create a file fallocate -l 1G test-bucket2.xyz Copy file to 2nd bucket aws s3 cp test-bucket2.xyz s3://<your-2nd-bucket-name> This operation succeeds because it is permitted by the VPC endpoint policy.
Then we test access to the first bucket by copy the file to 1st bucket aws s3 cp test-bucket2.xyz s3://<your-1st-bucket-name> This command will return an error because access to this bucket is not permitted by your new VPC endpoint policy.
Part 3 Summary: In this section, you created a VPC endpoint policy for Amazon S3, and used the AWS CLI to test the policy. AWS CLI actions targeted to your original S3 bucket failed because you applied a policy that only allowed access to the second bucket you created. AWS CLI actions targeted for your second bucket succeeded because the policy allowed them. These policies can be useful in situations where you need to control access to resources through VPC endpoints.

Secure Hybrid Access to S3 using VPC Endpoints Overview AWS PrivateLink provides private connectivity to AWS services from VPCs and your on-premises networks, without exposing your traffic to the Public Internet.
In this lab, you will learn how to create, configure, and test VPC endpoints that enable your workloads to reach AWS services without traversing the Public Internet.
You will create two types of endpoints to access Amazon S3: a Gateway VPC endpoint, and an Interface VPC endpoint. These two types of VPC endpoints offer different benefits depending on if you are accessing Amazon S3 from the cloud or your on-premises location
Gateway - Create a gateway endpoint to send traffic to Amazon S3 or DynamoDB using private IP addresses.You route traffic from your VPC to the gateway endpoint using route tables. Interface - Create an interface endpoint to send traffic to endpoint services that use a Network Load Balancer to distribute traffic. Traffic destined for the endpoint service is resolved using DNS.
